newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa maintain gains in abbreviated trading.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa maintain gains in abbreviated trading.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures maintained early gains by the finish on Friday in abbreviated trading ahead of a UK trade dinner.
Traders said weaker New York values came after London had closed. The London market will be closed on Monday for a local holiday, reopening on Tuesday
July stood six stg up at 994 stg a tonne by the close after ranging between 988 and 1,000, now seen as the immediate resistance.
Technically, the April 9 low of 980 stg remained a significant support. A break below that level could trigger more losses.
Cocoa dipped below the 1,000 stg mark for the first time since April 10 as speculators unloaded cocoa on a perception of mounting supplies.
Traders said there was some light industry interest this morning in reaction to an early slide in sterling against against the mark and dollar.
But by mid-morning sterling recouped some losses.
Overall volume reached a paltry 3,548 lots.
New York's July cocoa sagged to a low of $1,376 a tonne after triggering light sell-stops at $1,380. By 1629 GMT, it stood $10 down at $1,381.
Broker GNI said clearly the action of the past few days reflected the market's acceptance that supplies from Ivory Coast would be better than previously expected.
It also said the International Cocoa Organisation's revised production deficit estimate of 115,000 tonnes for 1996/97, down from its earlier estimate of 225,000 tonnes, was still seen as too high.
On Wednesday, GNI estimated the deficit at 33,000 tonnes. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
